subject.title: fix(memory-wiki): don't prune unsafe-local pages when a source path is   transiently unavailable

question: Should unsafe-local treat an unreadable explicitly configured file as a data-safety-preserving temporary outage, accepting retention of its stale imported page until configuration changes or the file returns?
rationale: The filesystem observation used here cannot distinguish an undocked or unmounted file source from a permanent deletion while preserving the existing no-new-config surface.

options.title: Accept conservative explicit-file retention
options.body: Land the scoped outage guard and accept that a still-configured explicit file remains represented until it is reachable again or removed from configuration.

options.title: Require an authoritative deletion design
options.body: Pause this PR until the plugin has a maintainer-approved way to distinguish intentional explicit-file deletion from a temporary unavailable path without reintroducing data loss.

recommendation.title: Accept conservative explicit-file retention
recommendation.body: Land the scoped outage guard and accept that a still-configured explicit file remains represented until it is reachable again or removed from configuration.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged source-page preservation work and adjacent prune-loss report make them the strongest available routing candidate for the page-retention contract.
